newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-SELES WINS CLAY COURT OPENER AT HILTON HEAD ISLAND.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SELES WINS CLAY COURT OPENER AT HILTON HEAD ISLAND.

text.p: Monica Seles shook the rust off her clay court strokes on Tuesday and scored a swift second-round victory over Shi-Ting Wang of Taiwan at the Family Circle Cup tennis tournament.
The fourth-seeded Seles, who received a first-round bye, posted a 6-3 6-3 win in 57 minutes.

"It was the first time I got to play some points on clay and I was pretty rusty starting off," said Seles, who reached the final on hard court at the Lipton Championships last week in her first tourament of the year.
"We had some nice rallie in there, so it was a good comfortable second round match," the fifth-ranked Seles said.
Seles was pleased with her progress after having her start to the season delayed while recuperating from a broken figure she suffered in December.
"I feel like I'm playing well comparing how many weeks I've played," Seles said, "but there's still a lot of work ahead of me if I want to be ready for the French (Open) and Wimbledon."
Fifth-seeded two-time champion Conchita Martinez of Spain had a much tougher time than Seles before pulling out a 6-7 6-4 6-3 second-round victory over qualifier Olga Barabanschikova of Belarus.

In a first-round encounter, Jennifer Capriati took another step forward in her halting comeback efforts by upsetting 11th-seeded fellow American Mary Joe Fernandez 6-3 4-6 7-6 in a match that featured 18 service breaks.
"Any time you play Jennifer it's a tough match and in the first round it's even tougher," Fernandez said.
The 21-year-old Capriati, who won the third-set tie-break 7-3, had reached the final here in 1990 as a 14-year-old.
"I'm glad I was able to pull it out because I think it's matches like that that really give you so much confidence that you can pull out those close ones," said the 28th-ranked Capriati.
Top seed Martina Hingis, who became the world's top-ranked player on Monday, was set to play the tournament's first-ever night match against Germany's Barbara Rittner later Tuesday.
